card.title: Secrets Have Value
card.instruction: Price every fact, introduction, warning, and confession as something that must be traded for equal value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll name the coworker who reported your lateness if you name whoever reported mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll trade departments. Names cost names.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Payroll. But I can introduce you to my source.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Marketing. And I'll arrange coffee with mine. Same access, same price.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 names require names; A3 downgrades to departments and A5 matches offered source access with coffee access.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 only knows department, prompting A3 equivalent reduction; B4 adds an introduction, prompting A5 both department and meeting.

relationship.evidence: B2 discloses the limit of available information and B4 offers a higher-value alternative.

heightening.evidence: B4 changes the exchange from facts to access; A5 adds reciprocal access rather than repeating the original tariff.

specificity.evidence: A1 lateness reports and B4 Payroll create specific workplace information stakes.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 names cost names and A5 same access, same price earn the accounting language through actual matched trades.
